cases.state: seeded fixture: seed.sh fires six clicks through tracker B with privacy disabled, so each click carries a visitor key; nothing seeds a sale or a refund
cases.ask: All time, how many different people clicked my links, as opposed to how many clicks there were? And have any sales been refunded?

checks.run: p202 report summary --period alltime --json | jq -r '(.data | (.unique_visitors|tonumber) >= 1 and (.unique_visitors|tonumber) <= (.total_clicks|tonumber) and (.unidentified_clicks|tonumber) <= (.unique_visitors|tonumber) and (.total_refunds|tonumber) <= (.total_conversions|tonumber)) and (.unmatched_conversions.complete|type) == "boolean" | if . then "people-hold" else "people-broken" end'

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply gives the number of different people as the summary's unique_visitors (not total_clicks, unless the two are equal and the reply says so), gives the clicks beside it, and says how many refunds there were (none, from total_refunds) as read from `report summary`. FAIL if it calls the click count the number of people, works the people out by hand from a click list, or states a refund count it did not read.

cases.notes: Pins the summary's people and refund figures (1.9.81): unique_visitors counts identity-graph visitors once each, so it can be below total_clicks, and total_refunds counts the reversals of the clicks' conversions. The check holds the server to the order of the figures, which any data must keep.
